A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the small intestinal mucosal microbiota is dysbiotic in patients with chronic liver disease, and is associated with increased intestinal permeability.
the duodenal mucosa-associated microbiome (MAM) is altered in chronic liver disease (CLDs), with a reduction in microbial diversity.
there is an inverse correlation between duodenal microbial diversity and both small intestinal barrier dysfunction and hepatic injury in patients with CLD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the small intestinal mucosal microbiota is altered in CLD, and this alteration is related to small intestinal permeability, a surrogate of intestinal barrier dysfunction.
the duodenal microbiota is associated with increased small intestinal permeabilty and liver injury in patients with chronic liver disease.
in chronic liver disease, the duodenal mucosa is colonized by microbes that are associated with small intestinal permeability, liver injury, and hepatic stiffness.
